description: Deep research agent to help you find the best GitHub repositories 🕵️!

summary.one_liner: DeepGit is an agentic research engine that finds GitHub repositories matching a natural-language request, judging candidates on evidence rather than raw keyword matches or star counts.
summary.what_it_does: It turns a free-form request into a search plan with angles, topics, must-have requirements, nice-to-haves and anti-patterns. It gathers candidates through batched GitHub GraphQL keyword queries and star-sorted topic sweeps. It keeps a local LanceDB + fastembed vector index of repos it has seen, so semantic recall improves over time (optional extra). A prefilter uses free signals like activity, license, tests/CI and relevance, then one LLM call ranks a shortlist. When the top picks are uncertain, it reads their source, tests and manifests, re-judges, and runs a reflection critic. Results are available as a Markdown report, a structured result object, a CLI command, or MCP tools.
use_cases: find the best GitHub repo for a specific library need
compare candidate open-source libraries before adopting one
search GitHub by language or hardware constraints
discover small well-matched repos beyond star-ranked results
let an AI assistant research repositories via MCP
how_to_run: deepgit search "a fast, embeddable key-value store in Go"
deepgit-mcp  # or: docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -e GITHUB_API_KEY=ghp_xxx deepgit
stack: LLM providers: groq, openai, anthropic, vertex_ai
notable: Adaptive agent: a confidence gate usually needs only about 2 LLM calls and escalates to real code-reading only for contested picks
Semantic recall via a local vector index that accumulates across searches
Enforces language and hardware constraints as hard requirements
First-class MCP server with tools for Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and similar clients
Ships a reproducible benchmark suite under bench/ with held-out results
caveats: Requires a GitHub personal access token and an LLM provider API key or Vertex AI credentials
Semantic recall needs the optional [semantic] extra (LanceDB + fastembed); without it only keyword and topic search run
Benchmark numbers come from a 12-query held-out set, so they are a small sample
